chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Salt, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah, and from al-Mufaddal ibn 'Umar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to connect what is between Sha'ban and Ramadan, and he would say: 'Fasting two consecutive months is a repentance from Allah.'

key_terms.تَوْبَة: Repentance (turning back to God, seeking forgiveness)
key_terms.رَمَضَان: Ramadan (the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, month of fasting)
key_terms.شَعْبَان: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar)
key_terms.صَوْم: Fasting (abstaining from food, drink, and other things from dawn to sunset)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of fasting between Sha'ban and Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi, transmitted through the chain of the Four Companions, underscores the spiritual significance of bridging Sha'ban and Ramadan with continuous fasting, a practice attributed to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin). It establishes the merit of fasting two consecutive months as a profound means of attaining divine repentance (tawbah), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercession of the Ahl al-Bayt in spiritual purification.
